title: Modern Toyota Hybrid Maintenance Is Simpler Than You Think
summary: The Car Care Nut demystifies practical maintenance on a modern Toyota/Lexus hybrid and an older LS430, focusing on coolant systems and fluids as well as non-routine repairs. The host demonstrates coolant service for both engine and inverter, identifies a dual-radiator setup within a single unit, drains radiators and transmission fluid, and then moves to a weatherstrip repair on the LS430 along with a rear-hatch shock motor swap. Throughout, the video emphasizes real-shop troubleshooting, tool selection (including a wobble socket for tight-clearance drains), and the importance of bleeding procedures and maintenance mode when servicing hybrids. The host also notes design quirks and safety considerations around high-voltage systems, offering practical guidance rather than relying on specialized diagnostics alone.
topics: Transmission fluid drain and fill (ATF WS)
Wobble socket for tight drain plug access
Bleeding and filling cooling system on hybrids

sections.title: Intro and plan
sections.description: Host introduces the shop day, outlines planned maintenance on a newer UX250h along with the older LS430: coolant for inverter and engine, transmission and differential fluids, and rear door shocks, plus a minor LS430 seal task.

sections.title: Hybrid platform and coolant identifiers
sections.description: Identification of the hybrid powertrain (M20A-FXS) and the coolant targets: inverter coolant and engine coolant, with note that removing the engine cover isn’t necessary for this work.

sections.title: Dual-radiator design explained
concepts: engine radiator vs inverter radiator drains
sections.description: Explanation that newer hybrids use a two-radiator setup within one unit, with separate drain paths for the engine and inverter circuits.

sections.title: Initial drains and transmission work
sections.description: Drain order begins with the lower radiator (less coolant), then proceeds to drain the transmission. The host notes the location of the drain and fill plugs and shares a quick anecdote about a prior GX470 service.

sections.title: LS430 weatherstrip repair with new clips
sections.description: The LS430 door weatherstrip seal is missing clips but intact; the team tests door operation and installs new retention clips to re-seat the seal, ensuring proper alignment.

sections.title: Transmission fill procedure and fluid type
sections.description: Transmission is filled with Lexus ATF WS (dual sections) until overflow, with attention to front and rear fill and expected capacity ranges.

sections.title: Hybrid vent behavior and differential vent
sections.description: Discussion of why hybrid transmissions use a spring-loaded vent rather than a continuously open vent, including a prior example of a leaking vent and its replacement.

sections.title: Wobble socket fix for a tight drain plug
sections.description: Demonstration of using a wobble socket to reach a stubborn drain plug in a tight space, illustrating why diverse tools are essential when engineers design for space constraints.

sections.title: Inverter bleed and maintenance mode prep
sections.description: Bleed procedure for the inverter coolant, including cycling the ignition and engine to move coolant and air, and preparing the system for final bleed under maintenance mode.

sections.title: Maintenance mode recap and safety reminders
sections.description: Recap of the hybrid maintenance mode steps, cautions about high-voltage safety, and final thoughts on performing diagnostic checks and safe run testing.

featured_techniques.technique: Hybrid coolant bleed procedure (engine and inverter) with staged fills
